questions.prompt: Can a function map two different inputs to the same output?
questions.explanation: x² maps −2 and 2 to 4; uniqueness is required per input.
options: Yes, provided each input has one output.
No, every output value must come from exactly one input, so outputs cannot repeat.

questions.explanation: Substitute x = −3: f(−3) = 2·(−3)² − 1. Square first: (−3)² = 9, then multiply: 2·9 = 18, then subtract: 18 − 1 = 17.

questions.prompt: Compute the sum of 2i for i = 1, 2, 3, that is 2·1 + 2·2 + 2·3.
A robot starts d₀ = 2 m from a wall and moves away at constant speed v = 3 m/s, so its distance is d(t) = d₀ + v·t. What is d after t = 4 s, in metres?
questions.explanation: d(4) = 2 + 3·4 = 2 + 12 = 14 m. Multiply before adding; m + (m/s)·s = m.

questions.prompt: Design a battery voltage-to-charge function. State what happens outside the measured range and why two batteries might require different parameters.
rubric: State the model, units, and assumptions.
Show the reasoning and an independently checkable result.
Name a failure case and a verification experiment.
